title_en: Cheng Hao v. Nanjing Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd., Jiangning Branch, et al. — dispute over liability of product manufacturer and seller
ruling_gist_en: Food products with labels lacking indication of ingredient content may be deemed as label-defective food. However, label-defective food is not equivalent to unsafe food. If a consumer claims ten times the price or three times the loss compensation on the ground of label defects pursuant to Article 148, paragraph 2 of the Food Safety Law of the PRC, the consumer shall further provide evidence to prove that the label-defective food has other circumstances that do not conform to food safety standards, or that the label defect affects food safety or misleads consumers.

full_text_en:
Cheng Hao v. Nanjing Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd. Jiangning Store et al.
— dispute over liability of product producer and seller

【Ruling Summary】

The lack of ingredient content labeling on a food label can be deemed as a defective food label, but a food with a defective label is not equivalent to unsafe food. Where a consumer claims compensation of ten times the price or three times the loss pursuant to the second paragraph of Article 148 of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China on the ground of a defect in the food label, the consumer shall continue to adduce evidence to prove that the food with the defective label has other circumstances of failing to meet food safety standards, or that the label defect has an impact on food safety or misleads the consumer.

Plaintiff: Cheng Hao, male, 47 years old, residing in Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Nanjing Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd. Jiangning Store, domiciled at Qinhuai Road, Jiangning Economic Development Zone, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Person in charge: Chen Qiuqing, Store Manager.

Defendant: Shandong Dong'e Ejiao Health Products Co., Ltd., domiciled at Ejiao Street, Dong'e County, Shandong Province.

Legal representative: Qin Yufeng, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiff, Cheng Hao, filed a lawsuit with the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province, against the defendants, Nanjing Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd. Jiangning Store (hereinafter referred to as "Auchan Supermarket") and Shandong Dong'e Ejiao Health Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Dong'e Company"), regarding a dispute over liability of product producer and seller.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On October 2, 2016, he purchased a total of 14 boxes of "Tao Hua Ji" Ejiao糕 (a type of health snack made from donkey-hide gelatin) produced by the defendant Dong'e Company from the defendant Auchan Supermarket at a unit price of RMB 279. Subsequently, he discovered that the product label did not indicate the content of donkey-hide gelatin (Ejiao), and both defendants were suspected of producing and selling unsafe food. Therefore, he filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting, in accordance with Articles 26, 67, and 148 of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, the return of the goods and a refund of the purchase price of RMB 3,906 from Auchan Supermarket, as well as compensation for losses of RMB 39,060, i.e., ten times the purchase price. Dong'e Company was requested to bear joint and several liability.

Defense of Defendants (Auchan Supermarket and Dong'e Company): (1) The plaintiff, Cheng Hao, is not a proper party in this case; he did not use his own bank card to purchase the products at issue, and Cheng Hao did not submit any other evidence to prove that he is the counterparty to the sales contract. (2) The products at issue meet food safety standards, and have the corresponding safety standard numbers and inspection reports. (3) Although the label of the product at issue does not indicate the content of donkey-hide gelatin (Ejiao), it does not specifically emphasize the characteristics of "Ejiao," so the label also complies with the provisions of relevant laws and regulations. In summary, the products at issue meet food safety standards and their labels are also compliant. The plaintiff's claims have no factual or legal basis and should be dismissed.

Facts Found by the Court at First Instance (Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City):

On October 2, 2016, the plaintiff, Cheng Hao, purchased 14 boxes of "Tao Hua Ji" Ejiao糕 food products, produced by the defendant Dong'e Company, from the defendant Auchan Supermarket, at a total price of RMB 3,906. The outer packaging of the food products bore the words "Tao Hua Ji Ejiao糕" in multiple places, with the characters "Ejiao糕" printed in red font. The ingredient list on the outer packaging indicated: "Walnut kernels, Black sesame seeds, Rice wine, High maltose syrup, Donkey-hide gelatin (Ejiao), Rock sugar, Maltodextrin," but did not indicate the content of any of these components. The execution standard was Q/DEB0002S, and the food production license number was QS371528011299. On October 20, 2015, Dong'e Company issued enterprise standard Q/DEB0002S-2015 for Ejiao糕 and filed it with the relevant government authority. On November 9, 2015, Dong'e Company obtained food production license number SC13137152407522, which listed the category name as "Other Foods" and the product variety details included "Ejiao糕 (Q/DEB0002S)." This food production license stated "Original production license number: QS371528011299." On June 13, 2014, the Shandong Provincial Food and Drug Administration issued a notice entitled "Notice of the Shandong Provincial Food and Drug Administration on Further Strengthening the Production Licensing of Ejiao糕-type Foods," which stated: "If the food label or food manual specifically emphasizes that one or more valuable or characteristic ingredients or components, such as donkey-hide gelatin (Ejiao) or black sesame seeds, have been added, the amount of addition or the content in the finished product of Ejiao and other raw materials should be indicated."

During the trial of this case at first instance, regarding the disputed evidence and facts, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City found as follows:

(1) Regarding whether the plaintiff, Cheng Hao, is a proper party. Cheng Hao submitted a marriage certificate, a bank card, and a credit card slip to prove that the bank card used for payment was owned by his spouse, Xue Peichun. The defendants Auchan Supermarket and Dong'e Company did not object to the authenticity of the above evidence, but argued that since the card was not owned by the plaintiff, it could not be proven that the plaintiff paid the purchase price, and the plaintiff was not the buyer under the sales contract. However, both defendants acknowledged that it was the plaintiff himself who used the card and signed the credit card slip.

(2) Regarding whether the "Tao Hua Ji" Ejiao糕 at issue is unsafe food. Dong'e Company submitted two inspection reports from the Liaocheng Food and Drug Inspection and Testing Center dated March 15, 2016, and September 18, 2016, respectively, to prove that the products at issue met food safety requirements. Both inspection reports showed that the samples of Tao Hua Ji Ejiao糕 submitted by Dong'e Company were tested in accordance with standard Q/DEB0002S-2015, and the tested items met the standard requirements. Cheng Hao did not object to the authenticity of the inspection reports, but argued that the inspection reports could not prove that the 14 boxes of Tao Hua Ji Ejiao糕 he purchased met the standard requirements. Cheng Hao also did not provide any other evidence to prove that the Ejiao糕 at issue did not meet food safety standards or posed a safety risk. Cheng Hao also acknowledged that he had not consumed the Ejiao糕 at issue and that it had not caused him any harm.

(3) Regarding whether the label of the Ejiao糕 at issue complied with the provisions of relevant laws and regulations. Dong'e Company submitted the "General Rules for the Labeling of Prepackaged Foods" (GB7718-2011), formulated and published by the health administrative department of the State Council on April 20, 2011, to prove that the label of the Ejiao糕 product at issue did not specifically emphasize the ingredient Ejiao, and therefore, in accordance with the above national standard, there was no need to indicate the content of Ejiao. Thus, the label of the product at issue complied with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance (Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province):

Parties have the responsibility to provide evidence to support their own claims. The evidence submitted by the plaintiff, Cheng Hao, including the physical Ejiao糕, the shopping receipt (invoice), and the bank card slip, is sufficient to prove that he purchased the Ejiao糕 at issue, produced by the defendant Dong'e Company, from the defendant Auchan Supermarket, and he is entitled to assert the claims at issue against both defendants. The sales contract for the Ejiao糕 at issue established between Cheng Hao and Auchan Supermarket was a true expression of their mutual intent, was lawful and valid, and is not altered by the method of payment used by Cheng Hao. The argument of both defendants that Cheng Hao is not a proper plaintiff in this case merely because he did not pay with a bank card owned by himself clearly has no factual or legal basis.

If a producer produces food that does not meet food safety standards, or a business operator knowingly sells food that does not meet food safety standards, consumers may, in addition to claiming compensation for losses, demand from the producer or business operator compensation of ten times the purchase price or three times the losses. However, this does not apply if the defects in the food label or manual do not affect food safety and do not mislead consumers. The Ejiao糕 product at issue bears the prominent words "Ejiao糕" in multiple places on the outer packaging. The argument of the defendants Auchan Supermarket and Dong'e Company that the product did not specifically emphasize "Ejiao" is clearly inconsistent with the facts. Ejiao has medicinal value and is an additive with specific value; according to regulations, its content should be indicated on the food label. The lack of an indication of Ejiao content on the label of the Ejiao糕 at issue constitutes a defect in the label. The plaintiff, Cheng Hao, is entitled to request the return of goods from Auchan Supermarket and a refund of the purchase price. Therefore, the court supports Cheng Hao's claim for the return of goods and a refund of RMB 3,906 from Auchan Supermarket. However, the Ejiao糕 at issue has obtained a food production license, and the relevant inspection reports also show that the product meets the production standards. Cheng Hao argues that the failure to indicate the "Ejiao" content on the label of the Ejiao糕 at issue poses a threat to food safety and creates a potential risk to consumers. However, a food with a defective label and unsafe food are not the same concept. Cheng Hao has not adduced further evidence to prove that the Ejiao糕 at issue does not meet food safety standards, nor can he prove that the label defect of the Ejiao糕 at issue affects food safety or would mislead consumers. Therefore, Cheng Hao's claim for ten times the purchase price compensation based on the label defect is not in accordance with the law. Thus, the court does not support Cheng Hao's claim for compensation of RMB 39,060 from Auchan Supermarket. Since the Ejiao糕 at issue is food with a defective label and does not meet the conditions for claiming ten times compensation as stipulated by law, the producer Dong'e Company also does not owe compensation to Cheng Hao. Furthermore, Dong'e Company is not the counterparty to the sales contract under which Cheng Hao purchased the Ejiao糕 at issue, so Cheng Hao is not entitled to request the return of goods or a refund from Dong'e Company. Therefore, the court does not support Cheng Hao's claim that Dong'e Company should bear joint and several liability for the debts of Auchan Supermarket.

Accordingly, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province, rendered the following judgment on December 14, 2016, pursuant to Article 60 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 26, 67, and the second paragraph of Article 148 of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China:

1. The defendant, Nanjing Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd. Jiangning Store, shall, within 10 days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, refund the purchase price of RMB 3,906 to the plaintiff, Cheng Hao. At the same time, the plaintiff, Cheng Hao, shall return the 14 boxes of "Tao Hua Ji" Ejiao糕 at issue to the defendant, Nanjing Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd. Jiangning Store.

2. The other claims of the plaintiff, Cheng Hao, are dismissed.

Cheng Hao, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, alleging: The evidence he provided at first instance was sufficient to prove that the Ejiao糕 at issue violated the mandatory provisions concerning food safety standards under the current Food Safety Law, and should therefore be deemed unsafe food. The court of first instance made an unclear finding of facts and improperly applied the law. Cheng Hao requested: The court of second instance should amend the judgment and order the appellees Auchan Supermarket and Dong'e Company to jointly and severally compensate the appellant RMB 39,060, i.e., ten times the purchase price.

Facts Found by the Court at Second Instance (Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province):

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province confirmed the facts found at first instance upon second instance trial.

During the second instance, the appellant, Cheng Hao, disagreed with the finding of the court of first instance that the failure to indicate the Ejiao content on the label of the product at issue constituted a label defect. He applied for an expert appraisal on whether the label identification of the product at issue complied with the requirements of GB7718-2011. The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held that the fact that the label identification of the product at issue did not comply with the requirements of GB7718-2011 could be confirmed and did not require expert appraisal. However, the fact that the product label does not meet food safety standards does not necessarily mean that it will affect food safety or mislead consumers. The court should review and determine this in accordance with the law. Therefore, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court did not allow Cheng Hao's application for expert appraisal.

Opinion of the Court at Second Instance (Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province):

The focal point of dispute at second instance is: Does the fact that the label of the Ejiao糕 at issue does not meet food safety standards affect food safety or mislead consumers?

(1) Regarding whether it affects food safety. According to the facts found, the manufacturer of the food at issue, the appellee Dong'e Company, has obtained a production license issued by the state, and the submitted samples of the food at issue were also tested and found qualified by the Liaocheng Food and Drug Inspection and Testing Center. Apart from pointing out that the label of the Ejiao糕 at issue did not indicate the Ejiao content, the appellant, Cheng Hao, has no contrary evidence to prove that the label of the food at issue affected food safety or that the food at issue caused personal harm to him.

(2) Regarding whether it misleads consumers. The "Tao Hua Ji" Ejiao糕 at issue is an ordinary food. In the product ingredient list, Ejiao is listed after ingredients such as walnut kernels, black sesame seeds, rice wine, and high maltose syrup. Dong'e Company did not particularly emphasize or exaggerate the Ejiao component in the product label or instructions. Therefore, although Dong'e Company did not indicate the specific content of Ejiao on the label, this defect is insufficient to mislead consumers in their purchase decisions. Consequently, although the product at issue has a label defect, this defect does not affect the safety of the food and does not mislead consumers. The court of first instance's decision not to support Cheng Hao's claim for ten times compensation was appropriate.

In summary, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Article 170, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on March 13, 2017:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
